title: The Boy Who Planted a Forest
summary: Inspired by a school lesson, a boy plants one tree at a time on a barren hillside, and over the years his small effort grows into a real community forest.
poll: One person's small effort, kept up over many years, can grow into something much bigger than they imagined.

versions.title: The Boy Who Planted a Forest
versions.text:
Saeed is at school. His teacher talks about trees. Trees help the land and the animals.

Near Saeed's home is a bare hill. No trees grow there. The hill is just rock and sand.

Saeed wants to help. He asks his dad for a small tree. His dad says yes.

They walk up the hill. Saeed digs a hole in the soil. He puts the small tree in the hole. He adds water.

Saeed goes up the hill every day. He gives the tree water. The tree grows slowly.

The next year, Saeed plants one more tree. Then he plants another. Soon there are five trees on the hill.

A neighbor sees the trees. She wants to help too. She brings a tree of her own to plant.

More neighbors come to help. They all plant trees on the hill. They all bring water too.

Years go by. The bare hill is now full of trees. Birds live in the trees now.

What was one boy's small plan grew into a real forest. All the neighbors feel proud of their forest.

versions.title: The Boy Who Planted a Forest
versions.text:

What began as one boy's small plan had grown into a real community forest. Every neighbor who helped felt proud of what they had built together.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?

A boy who moves far away from his home
questions.why: The whole story follows Saeed as he plants trees on the bare hill until it becomes a forest.

wrong.C: The story is about trees, not finding water underground.
wrong.D: Saeed does not move away in the story.

His teacher talks about how trees help the land and animals
He wants a place to hide from his family

MID.prompt: Explain how Saeed's small effort of planting one seedling eventually grew into a shared community forest. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how Saeed's effort grew over time.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Saeed's effort started small when he planted just one seedling on the barren hill and watered it every day until it grew. The next year he added a native tree, and soon a neighbor noticed the young trees and brought her own sapling to plant beside his. More neighbors kept joining after seeing this happen, until the whole community was planting trees together. Over many years, this shared effort turned the once-barren hill into a real community forest.

keyWords.definition: to care for and help something grow
keyWords.example: Farmers cultivate rice in flooded fields.

keyWords.definition: the gradual wearing away of soil or rock, often by wind or water
keyWords.example: Tree roots help slow down erosion on a hillside.

keyWords.definition: the wide variety of living things found in a particular area
keyWords.example: Rainforests contain some of the richest biodiversity on Earth.

keyWords.definition: the quality of continuing to try, even when something is hard
keyWords.example: Learning a new language takes real perseverance.

keyWords.definition: to bring something back to a good or healthy condition
keyWords.example: Volunteers worked for years to restore the damaged wetland.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says one person's small effort, kept up over many years, can grow into something much bigger than they imagined. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that one person's small effort, kept up over many years, can grow into something much bigger than they imagined. Saeed started with just one seedling on a barren hill, but his perseverance in watering it daily, combined with his choice to plant native species, eventually caught his neighbors' attention. Because he kept going year after year, a single neighbor's sapling turned into a full community effort that restored the entire hillside and even inspired other communities to attempt similar projects. Someone might argue that Saeed alone could never have created a whole forest, but the story shows that his consistent, modest actions were exactly what made the larger community effort possible in the first place.
